name: Chakravartin (Fisherking Archetype)
body:
While most fisherkings are merely sovereigns of their own domains, an exalted few are more akin to a cogwheel of the cosmos’ celestial machinery. Chakravartin are wise fisherkings who have yoked the might of the heavens to their will, and bring cosmic order to all they survey.

Manifester of Cosmic Law

A fisherking must have an alignment of lawful good or lawful neutral to take this archetype.

Aura of Law (Ex)

The power of a chakravatin’s aura of law (see the detect law spell) is equal to their fisherking level.

Static Servants

The color and markings of the livery worn by chakravartin’s royal attendants is selected the first time that one is summoned and can only be changed when the chakravartin gains a new level in the fisherking class. This ability alters royal attendants.

Constellations

Chakravartin learn to call on the constellations for power starting at 1st level. The constellations that they can manifest are drawn from a single cosmology of their choice that they select when gaining this ability. They use Wisdom as their starcalling modifier. The saving throw

DCs for their constellations is 10+1/2 their starcaller level + their starcalling modifier unless stated otherwise. This ability replaces veilweaving, and chakra binds.

Cosmology

At 1st level, the chakravartin must select a cosmology to attune themselves to. This must be a cosmology that is tied to their current plane of existence. They must also select any lost constellations or lesser cosmologies that they wish to access at this time (subject to the customization limit rule). Once they have chosen a cosmology, they cannot manifest constellations from another cosmology without taking the Expanded Cosmology feat. If they spend at least one month in a plane with a different cosmology than the one they chose, they may choose to realign themselves with the new cosmology, losing access to their previous cosmology and constellations and gaining access to those available in the new cosmology. Additionally, they gain a competence bonus equal to their starcalling modifier to identify constellation manifestations that are a part of their cosmology.

GM Advice?Tuning the Astradhari

For some games, the sheer possibilities of astra summoning might be too much to handle. In that case, it is recommended that the Gamemaster makes premade lists of enhancement and fighting style feats (and souls or disciplines in the case of the archetypes), for every astra available in their games.

All as One (Su)

All of the champion forms of the chakravartin’s constellations have a single shared pool of health points equal to 1d6 + their starcalling modifier, per starcaller level (the 1st d6 is maximized). This replaces any hit points that champions would normally have from HD and class levels, but does not alter their HD total for the purposes of effects based on their number of HD. Any effects that add to or subtract from a champion’s hit points (e.g. the Toughness feat, the essence effect of The Boar’s champion form, or Constitution damage) are applied to this shared pool for the effect’s duration on until the champion that is the source of the effect is dismissed, whichever happens first. Constitution damage, drain, or increases taken by a champion alter the shared pool’s maximum hit points while the affected champion is summoned as if the score that determines the chakravartin’s starcalling modifier had been had taken damage or drain, or been increased by the same amount.

All damage, healing, and temporary hit points received by champions are deducted from or added to this shared pool. When the pool is reduced to 0 or below, all champions manifested by the chakravartin are dismissed, and may not be manifested again until the pool is returned to a positive value. If this shared pool has been reduced to 0, it is automatically restored to half of its normal maximum value after 24 hours.

Champions count as a single entity for beneficial abilities that may only be used on a creature a limited number of times a day (e.g. a witch’s healing hex). Should multiple champions take damage from the same attack or effect, the damage is only applied to the shared hit point pool once as if it had only affected the champion that would have taken the most damage.

Life Link (Su)

At 1st level, the chakravartin forms a close bond with their champions. As long as the chakravartin and at least one of their manifested champions are within 100 feet of each other, whenever enough damage would be dealt to their champions’ shared hit point pool to dismiss their champions, as a reaction to the damage, the chakravartin can sacrifice any number of hit points they have without using an action. Each hit point sacrificed in this way prevents 1 point of damage dealt to their champions’ shared hit point pool. This can prevent champions from being dismissed.

Enlightened Hexes

A chakravartin uses Wisdom instead of Charisma to determine the difficulty class of their hexes.

Royal Voice

At 1st level, chakravartin gain Viceroy as a bonus feat. At 9th level they gain Regency as a bonus feat. They use Wisdom as their veilweaving modifier for the veil gained in this way. They gain these feats even if they do not meet the prerequisites. If they already possess these feats or the ability to shape and bind Voice veils from another source they can instead choose to gain an akashic feat of their choice that they meet the prerequisites for at these levels.

They can not gain the ability to shape a Voice veil with the chaotic descriptor using this ability.

Divine Presence

The chakravartin’s class levels count as divine caster levels instead of arcane caster levels. A chakravartin with the king’s cup hex, crafts potions using spells drawn from the cleric spell list that could be cast by a cleric of their fisherking level. This ability alters arcane presence.

Devarajah (Su)

The chakravartin is a channel through which divine order can suffuse the world. As a swift action the chakravartin can activate a 30-foot radius aura centered on themself that causes the world to be reshaped by their divine right to rule. This effect ends if the chakravartin is knocked unconscious or if they choose to end it as a swift action. At the start of each day, the chakravartin can select one of the following effects for this aura. Creatures within the area of the aura, other than themself, gain bonuses or take penalties depending on the effect selected, as indicated below:

Blessing

Allies, and creatures with an attitude of indifferent or better towards the chakravartin, within this aura gain a +1 sacred bonus to skill checks, Fortitude saving throws, and Constitution checks to resist non-lethal damage from exhaustion, hunger, or thirst. At 5th and 13th levels, this bonus to saving throws and checks increases by +1.

Order

Lawful descriptor effects within this aura increase their DCs by +1 and chaotic descriptor effects take a – 1 penalty to their DCs. Additionally, when selecting this effect for their aura the chakravartin must roll a number of d20s equal to their Wisdom modifier and record the results as a pool to use later. As an immediate action when an ally, other than themself, within the radius of this aura fails a skill check, attack roll, or saving throw they can replace that d20 roll with one of the recorded rolls, removing that roll from the pool.

Alternatively, as an immediate action when an enemy within the radius of this aura succeeds on a skill check, attack roll, or saving throw the chakravartin can replace their d20 roll with one of the recorded rolls, which removes that roll from the pool. An unwilling target can make a Will saving throw against the chakravartin’s hex DC. If they succeed, the roll is resolved as normal, and the roll selected to replace it is still removed from the pool. Any rolls still remaining in the pool at the start of the next day are lost. At 5th and 13th levels the DC increases and penalties of this aura increase by +1. This ability may be invested with essence, increasing the granted aura’s radius by 5 feet for each point of essence invested. For every two points of essence invested in this ability any bonuses or penalties caused by this ability are increased by 1. This does not increase the bonuses granted by this ability at 9th level.

At 9th level, the chakravartin’s aura increases to a 60-foot radius. In addition, the chakravartin gains a sacred bonus to Perception and Sense Motive against targets within the area of their aura equal to 1 + the number of points of essence invested in this ability.

At 17th level, the chakravartin’s aura increases to a 90-foot radius. This ability replaces blessed land and the blessed land improvements gained at 9th and 17th levels.

Maya Hexes

At 3rd level, the chakravartin learns how to summon physical manifestations of their hexes through a constellation that only they can conjure called The Maya. This constellation is added to their cosmology and can’t be replaced by a lost constellation or by gaining a lesser cosmology.

New Chakravartin Hexes

The following hexes are available to fisherkings with the chakravartin archetype.

Celestial Rajah (Major Hex; Su): The chakravartin’s ability to manipulate the constellations and filter out incompatible energies increases even further, reducing their essence penalty for manifesting constellations with opposing elements from 2 to 1. Additionally, they reduce the essence cost to manifest one form of a constellation in their cosmology by 1 to a minimum of 1. This can be changed once per day by spending an hour in meditation. They must have the celestial nawab hex to take this major hex. This hex can’t be selected as a part of manifesting the Maya constellation.
Celestial Nawab (Hex; Su): The chakravartin becomes more skilled at shaping and purifying the energies of constellations and reduce the essence penalty they take for manifesting constellations with opposing elements from 3 to 2. Additionally, they reduce the essence cost to manifest one form of a constellation in their cosmology by 1 to a minimum of 1. The selected form can be changed once per day by spending an hour in meditation. They must be at least 8th level to take this hex. This hex can’t be selected as a part of manifesting the Maya constellation.
Celestial Maharaja (Grand; Su): The chakravartin no longer pay an essence penalty for manifesting constellations with opposing elements. Additionally, they reduce the essence cost to manifest one form of a constellation in their cosmology by 1 to a minimum of 1. The selected form can be changed once per day by spending an hour in meditation. They must have the celestial rajah hex to take this grand hex. This hex can not be selected as a part of manifesting the Maya constellation.
Ex-Chakravartin

A chakravartin that gains a chaotic alignment, who willfully commits a chaotic act, loses the ability to use all alternate class features granted by this archetype except for royal voice and divine presence (but still retains all other fisherking class features). They also lose access to any hexes that require this archetype. Though they are still considered to be a chakravartin when taking further levels in the fisherking class. A chakravartin regains use of all archetype alternate class features and unique hexes if they atone for their violations (see the atonement spell).
